Transductive label spreading on a hypergraph

Source: R/hypergraph_laplacian.R
hypergraph_transduction.Rd

hypergraph_transduction() classifies the unlabelled nodes of a hypergraph from a few labelled ones, by the label-spreading framework of Zhou et al. (2006). The labels spread over the hypergraph as the scores $$F = (1 - \xi) (I - \xi S)^{-1} Y,$$ where \(S = I - L\) is the similarity operator of the chosen Laplacian (see hypergraph_laplacian()) and \(Y\) marks each labelled node's class, and each node is assigned the class with the highest score. This is the non-neural ancestor of hypergraph-attention text classifiers: with documents as hyperedges over words (or the reverse), it classifies unlabelled nodes from a handful of labelled ones.

The margin of a node, its winning minus its runner-up score, says how clearly it was assigned; assignments with a small margin are the ones to distrust. The given labels are not held fixed, so a labelled node can be predicted into another class, and a class's scores grow with its number of labelled nodes. As xi approaches 1, every node's scores become proportional to the same vector, so in the limit every node is assigned the same class. On a small hypergraph the default 0.99 can come close to that; compare the predictions under a smaller xi.

Usage

hypergraph_transduction(
  hg,
  labels,
  xi = 0.99,
  type = c("zhou", "random_walk"),
  edge_weights = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_hypergraph_transduction'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_hypergraph_transduction'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_hypergraph_transduction'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  what = c("predictions", "scores"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'net_hypergraph_transduction'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

hg

The hypergraph: a connected net_hypergraph, as for hypergraph_laplacian().

labels

The known class labels, in one of two forms: a vector named by node, covering some of the nodes, or an unnamed vector with one entry per node, in the hypergraph's node order, and NA for the unlabelled ones. Required. It must hold at least two distinct classes; a name that is not a node, or an unnamed vector of the wrong length, raises an error.

xi

The spreading coefficient, a number strictly between 0 and 1. Larger values give the hypergraph structure more weight relative to the given labels. Default 0.99.

type, edge_weights

The Laplacian and its hyperedge weights, passed to hypergraph_laplacian(). Defaults "zhou" and NULL.

x

For the print(), as.data.frame() and plot() methods: a net_hypergraph_transduction object.

...

For the methods: ignored.

object

For the summary() method: a net_hypergraph_transduction object.

row.names

For the as.data.frame() method: row names for the returned data frame. Default NULL keeps the default row numbers.

optional

For the as.data.frame() method: ignored; it is there to match the base::as.data.frame() generic.

what

For the as.data.frame() method: the table to return. "predictions" (default) gives one row per node; "scores" gives one row per node and class.

Value

A net_hypergraph_transduction object. print() reports the Laplacian, xi, the classes and how many nodes each was predicted for; summary() returns one row per class; plot() draws the node-by-class score heatmap. The object's fields:

predictions

A data frame with one row per node: node, label (the given label, NA for an unlabelled node), predicted, score (the winning class's score) and margin (the winning minus the runner-up score).

classes

The classes, sorted.

scores

The node-by-class score matrix.

xi, type

The spreading coefficient and the Laplacian type.

n_labeled, n_nodes

The numbers of labelled and of all nodes.

params

The edge_weights used.

The print() method returns its input invisibly. The summary() method returns a data frame with one row per class: class, n_labeled, n_predicted and mean_margin (the mean margin of the nodes predicted into the class, NA when there are none). The as.data.frame() method returns, for what = "predictions", one row per node with node, label (NA for an unlabelled node), predicted, score and margin, and for what = "scores" one row per node and class with node, class and score. The plot() method returns the score heatmap as a ggplot, visibly, so plot(x) draws it: one row per node, grouped by predicted class and ordered by margin within it, one column per class, the tiles shaded and labelled by score. Labelled nodes have a black border on their given class, and a dot marks each node's winning class, so seeds, scores and assignments can be compared in one panel.

References

Zhou, D., Huang, J., & Schölkopf, B. (2006). Learning with hypergraphs: Clustering, classification, and embedding. NeurIPS 19.

Examples

events <- data.frame(
  person = c("a", "b", "c", "a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f",
             "d", "e", "f", "c", "d"),
  meeting = c("m1", "m1", "m1", "m2", "m2", "m2", "m3", "m3", "m3",
              "m4", "m4", "m4", "m5", "m5")
)
hg <- bipartite_groups(events, player = "person", group = "meeting")
tr <- hypergraph_transduction(hg, labels = c(a = "x", d = "y"))
tr
#> Hypergraph transductive label spreading (zhou Laplacian, xi = 0.99)
#>   Nodes: 6 (2 labeled) | Classes: x, y
#>   Predicted: x = 1, y = 5
as.data.frame(tr)
#>   node label predicted     score      margin
#> 1    a     x         x 0.1654808 0.003987167
#> 2    b  <NA>         y 0.1614936 0.006012833
#> 3    c  <NA>         y 0.2037821 0.019834793
#> 4    d     y         y 0.2321154 0.070621782
#> 5    e  <NA>         y 0.1839473 0.055966489
#> 6    f  <NA>         y 0.1839473 0.055966489
